configs.description: Dual 920W AC PSUs (PSU-921-AECR1) 1+1, dual FAN-402825-HDN fan modules 1+1, front-to-back airflow - the only offered build
configs.name: ac

gaps.note: 'FAN ◄0' / 'FAN ◄1' appear at the top of each fan module's right strip in both the HIG rear figure and the photograph. If they are chassis printing they are hidden behind the modules; if module printing, the shared fan-402825 component cannot carry a per-position digit. A photo of the bay with the module out would settle which metal carries the ink.
gaps.wanted: photograph of an empty S6301-56STP fan bay.

gaps.note: the HIG says 'there are two locations on the case in which the grounding lug may be fixed' and Figure 20 shows one under a yellow peel-off label on a side wall, but no held source shows its position measurably; only the rear location (Figure 21, photographed) is modelled.
gaps.wanted: a photograph or drawing locating the second lug position.

gaps.note: ufispace/fan-402825 states no draw and its own contract records the search: eight UfiSpace datasheets name the part only as an ordering line, with no wattage anywhere near it; this device's HIG likewise dimensions and weighs the fan FRU and tables its LED without a power figure. L29's standing warning is the live count of how much of the chassis total is a floor.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the fan module's label, or a UfiSpace FRU datasheet.

gaps.note: datasheet '1 x USB 1.0 Type-A port'; HIG cabling section 'Connect the USB 2.0 A Type plug'; HIG accessory list ships a 'USB 3.0 cable'. Same port, three versions. The manifest carries the datasheet's line and says so.
gaps.wanted: vendor confirmation of the actual USB controller version.

gaps.note: the HIG front-panel table defines only the MODE-level meaning ('LED on each network port indicates the link & speed status' / 'the PoE status') and no per-colour vocabulary for the SFP+ lamps; the sfp-led-pair placements carry that mode-switched reading and nothing finer. PoE mode is meaningless for the SFP+ ports and the vendor does not say what they show then.
gaps.wanted: a NOS LED table or photographs of a live unit in known port states.
the buried marks moved clear of the components that paint over them

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor
`physical-context` on 4 bays (rear 4); `physical-context` on port groups ge-poe, sfp-plus - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

attrs.note: datasheet (Specifications table and Supported Accessories), with the HIG Connecting Power section for the system maxima and the PoE budget

bottom.note: deliberately size-only - no photograph or drawing of the underside exists in the intake (the HIG's Figure 5 shows top, front and rear only), and inventing the label field the class of device usually carries would be a guess. L45's size-only warning stands as the record.

buttons.note: drawing - MODE at (37.4, 4.4) and RESET at (47.1, 4.4), legends under each, read from HIG Figure 8; both drawn with common/reset-button (4 mm recessed pinhole). The real MODE button is a raised rubber dome ~4 mm - closest library part used and the delta recorded here. Mode function per the HIG LED table footnote: 'The Mode button on the front panel allows switching between LNK/SPD and PoE status LEDs'.

chassis.note: datasheet - 'Chassis (WxDxH) 1RU, 440 x 440 x 43.8 mm', weight 5.74 kg without FRU; the HIG Component Physical Information table repeats all three. 440 is the body between the ear folds, not a rack face: the HIG Space Clearance section separates 'The S6301-56STP width is 17.32 inches (44.0cm)' from the 'rack mount brackets suitable for 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks', and the brackets are shipped loose (88 x 43 x 20 mm accessories, 8 M4 screws), so no ear extent needed subtracting. Depth 440 is likewise 'without the field replaceable units (FRUs)'; the fan handles project 25 mm and the PSU handles 38 mm beyond it (HIG Space Clearance), carried as relief on the FRU contracts rather than in the chassis depth.

front-layout.note: drawing - HIG Figure 8 (Port Overview strip, 1385 x 141 px). GATE 1: the chassis in it measures 1378 x 137 px, aspect 10.06 against the datasheet's 10.05 (440/43.8) - 0.1% out, orthographic, measured at 3.13 px/mm. The 48 RJ45 jacks sit in four 6-column ganged blocks: the green jack LEDs (one per jack, read as column markers) give a within-block pitch of 13.9 mm and a block step of 87.5 mm (three independent steps of 87.49), first jack left edge at x 25.8. The SFP+ block's blue paint spans x 376.1-434.3, four columns on the std 14.25 pitch. Vent strip holes run x 84.6-436.5 in two rows. Vertical placements are the softer axis: the figure draws the jack rows schematically short, so the rows are set inside the measured shell band (y 11.9-38.3) with std/rj45-ganged's 11.0 height and the row split recorded here as drawing-constrained rather than measured.

jack-orientation.note: photo - the front photograph and the datasheet front render, zoomed: the TOP RJ45 row has its keyway/tab UP and gold contacts toward the centre band (rotate 180 from the std default), the bottom row keyway-down; the SFP+ top row's nubs face the centre lamp band and the bottom row's face it from below - belly-to-belly, so the bottom row carries rotate: 180 under the library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S3: upper rotate 0 over lower 180, both bails outward). Same mirrored-rows construction as the GL-8XEP and MX150 precedents.

jack-shells.note: photo-measured - the four 12-port RJ45 blocks sit in SILVER ganged shells on the real unit (product render s6301-56stp-2-front.png); std/rj45-ganged draws the opening only, so each block's shell is a decor fill sized from its own placements plus a 1.1/1.2 mm flange, per the s9510-28dc silver-band precedent. Caught in review after the first pass drew the jacks dark-on-dark - the same defect the gl-8xep review found, and one no lint rule can see.

left-cluster.note: drawing - HIG Figure 8 at 3.13 px/mm: silver bezel plate x 6.4-21.7, y 4.2-39.3 holding, top to bottom, the OOB management jack (two lamps above it), the USB-A port and the console jack ('IOIO' legend, HIG section 11: 'The console can be connected using the RJ45 port labelled IOIO'). The management and console jacks are drawn with std/rj45-ganged inside the shared plate decor because the plate is one piece of metal - the 16 mm single-port bezels would not fit the 35 mm stack. Management jack keyway-up (rotate 180), console keyway-down, both read from the figure's tab notches at zoom. The left-edge network pictogram and the USB/LED-mode/IOIOI icon row are approximated with the nearest glyphs, as the S9510-28DC does.

lifecycle.note: searched 2026-08-28, 'UfiSpace S6301-56STP end of life' - no announcement; the vendor still lists the product (ufispace.com S6301-56STP product page) and it joined the SONiC Lite HCL in Feb 2026. none-announced is a checked state, not an absence.

port-leds.note: photo+HIG - each RJ45 jack carries ONE integrated lamp in its outer corner (top-left on the top row, bottom-left on the bottom row), mode-switched between LNK/SPD and PoE status by the front-panel Mode button (HIG front panel LED table). Before the RJ45 sweep std/rj45-ganged drew the opening only and the lamps, sitting INSIDE the jack apertures, were not drawn - same treatment as the MX150's in-jack lamps. They now draw as led-a/led-b of common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 on the ge-poe group (both corners modelled at component default vocabulary; the mode-switched single-lamp behaviour the hardware actually has is not separately captured here). The SFP+ ports' lamps sit in the centre band between the cage rows (one ▲▼ pair per column, upper/lower port) and are drawn with common/sfp-led-pair, states overridden to the mode-switched vocabulary because the component default cites another device's guide.

port-numbering.note: HIG Port Overview table: 'Port ID 0~47 RJ45 ... 48~55 SFP+', and the printed strip under each column pair reads '▲n  n+1▼' (even numbers top row, odd bottom). HIG Figure 8 draws large per-jack numerals as a schematic aid; the photographs show NO numerals on the ganged shells - the real device numbers its ports only on the strip below the field, so only the strip is modelled (guide art vs real device: the real device wins).

power.note: datasheet gives 'Typical power: 80 Watts (no transceiver)'. The HIG Connecting Power section gives the maxima: 'The maximum system power consumption is 145 watts without PoE enabled, and 1517 watts with PoE enabled', with the testing criteria printed beside them - 45C ambient, optics fully populated, 100% traffic load - hence power-envelope: fully-configured. power-max-w carries the PoE-enabled 1517; the no-PoE 145 is kept as power-max-no-poe-w because the two describe the same box with and without its defining feature loaded. The PoE budget is stated three times as 820 W (802.3at 30 W or 802.3af 15.4 W per port). The vendor qualifies all of these; nothing here is an unqualified reading.

psu-fru.note: ufispace/psu-921-ac@1 built for this device from the HIG Fig 6 drawing, Component Physical Information table and the rear photograph; the fan FRU reuses ufispace/fan-402825@1 (S9510-28DC family) - the datasheet orders FAN-402825-HDN where the S9510 orders -HD, same drawn 51.5 x 42.2 face, and the configuration overrides the model attr. The S6301 photo shows the fan status lamp low on the right strip where the component draws it top-left - a skin-level delta on a shared part, recorded here and left

rear-layout.note: drawing - HIG Figure 7 rear strip (1391 x 143 px, aspect 10.11 vs true 10.05, 0.6% out, 3.15 px/mm): grounding column at the left edge (two M4 holes at (6.2, 7.6) and (6.2, 24.4) with the earth symbol below - one of the HIG's two lug locations, Figure 21), fan bays at x 13.7 and 65.9 (module faces 51.5 x 42.2 abutting), blank panel to x 277, PSU bays at x 277.2 and 360.5 (faces 73 x 40 confirmed by the red release tabs at 340.9-350.1 and 424.1-433.0), vertical 'PSU0 ◄'/'PSU1 ◄' legends on the chassis strips right of each bay. The photograph corroborates every feature. The 'FAN ◄0'/'FAN ◄1' texts sit ON the fan modules' own faces in both sources, not on the chassis, and the shared fan component cannot carry a per-position legend - not modelled, see gaps.

sides.note: estimated - no orthographic side drawing exists; the angle photograph shows the LEFT side with the front bracket screw holes and rear rail holes, and positions are estimated from it against the HIG accessory dimensions (bracket 88 x 43 x 20 mm with 4 M4 holes; rail 406.8 x 43 x 21 mm). AXIS CONVENTION: on the RIGHT view x = 0 is the FRONT; on the LEFT view x = 0 is the REAR (renderer convention). Content is otherwise symmetric hole patterns, mirrored as depth - x - width.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the reading of the cages recorded in this provenance: the 4 SFP pairs (port-48/port-49 to port-54/port-55). 4 of these were drawn with the upper cage turned before the std cage art moved its lip to the bottom of the opening; turning them keeps the lips in the middle band where they were drawn and seats every optic bail-outward.

system-leds.note: drawing - HIG Figure 8: two lamp rows above the first jack block, row 1 at y ~4.5 (SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1 at x 53.6/60.5/67.2/74.0), row 2 at y ~7.1 (LNK/SPD, POE, ID at x 53.0/66.5/73.2), lamps ~1.3 mm drawn with common/led-dot (2.0 mm, nearest part). States transcribed from the HIG section 10 front-panel LED table on each placement.

top.note: drawing - HIG Figure 5 top view (D and W both dimensioned 440 mm; measured at 1.44 px/mm against them). AXIS: y = 0 is the REAR, as the figure is printed (fan handles and PSU tabs at its top edge). Four recessed finger-slot grooves at y 132/212/293/370 from the rear (the two nearer the rear span x 190-433, the two nearer the front x 10-433) plus the screw heads the figure draws. Positions to the figure's ~1 mm; groove depth not dimensioned anywhere, drawn as sink decor.

usb-version.note: sources-disagree, recorded not resolved: the datasheet says '1 x USB 1.0 Type-A port', the HIG's cabling section says 'Connect the USB 2.0 A Type plug', and the accessory list ships a 'USB 3.0 cable'. The manifest carries the datasheet's line verbatim; see gaps. THE DRAWING FOLLOWS THE MANIFEST, not the cable: the `usb2` skin paints USB-IF's white tongue, which is the colour for 1.x AND 2.0, so it agrees with two of the three sources at once and leaves the disagreement where it is. The blue it drew before agreed only with the accessory cable, and nothing in the library had chosen that.
